Full time role)

Must have Skills - 6-10
years Data Validation& Validation & AWS Data services (Redshift, Lake Formation, Athena, and S3-based data lakes), Python, ETL ELT concepts, QA methodology (Test planning & design, Defect lifecycled.

Data Validation & Verification

Validate transformation logic against business rules and documented specifications
Perform source-to-target data reconciliation — verifying completeness, accuracy, and consistency
Identify data anomalies, silent failures, and drift in pipeline outputs
Build and maintain automated data validation suites that execute as part of pipeline runs
Conduct periodic data audits beyond automated checks

QA Process Definition & Governance

Define acceptance criteria
for each ETL pipeline and transformation step — establishing what "correct" means in measurable, testable terms
Define Definition of Done (DoD)
for all data deliverables — specifying when a pipeline output is considered production-ready
Create and maintain data quality test plans
covering functional correctness, edge cases, regression, and performance
Design test cases
for new transformations before they reach production (shift-left testing)
Establish data quality SLAs
— freshness, completeness, and accuracy thresholds
Define entry and exit criteria
for pipeline releases — what must pass before promoting changes
Maintain a defect taxonomy
— categorizing data issues (schema drift, logic errors, source issues, timing issues) for root cause tracking and trend analysis
Define sign-off workflows
— who approves what before data reaches the UI layer

Test Strategy & Frameworks

Design the overall data testing strategy:
Unit tests
for individual transformation logic
Integration tests
for end-to-end pipeline correctness
Regression tests
for ongoing stability
Smoke tests
for post-deployment verification
Negative tests
for resilience (nulls, duplicates, out-of-range values, schema violations)
Build reusable, parameterized validation patterns applicable across multiple pipelines
Implement data contract validation — ensuring upstream sources meet agreed schemas and value constraints
Integrate quality gates into CI/CD pipelines for automated release blocking

Documentation & Traceability

Document expected behavior for each transformation (input, logic, expected output)
Maintain data quality runbooks — investigation and resolution procedures for common issues
Create traceability matrices linking business requirements to test cases to pipeline outputs
Document known data limitations, assumptions, and technical debt
Maintain a living catalog of data quality rules and their rationale

Monitoring, Observability & Reporting

Build data quality dashboards tracking pass/fail rates, trend analysis, and SLA compliance
Configure alerting for data quality threshold breaches
Track and report data quality metrics (DQ score, defect density, mean time to detect, mean time to resolve)
Conduct data quality retrospectives — identifying gaps and improving coverage

Collaboration

Participate in pipeline design reviews — flagging quality risks early in development
Work with product and business stakeholders to translate vague requirements into testable assertions
Collaborate with data engineers on pipeline improvements driven by quality findings
Support UI/frontend teams in verifying rendered data correctness

jobs.title: Data Analyst
jobs.description:
Job Summary

This position is in the District Department of Transportation (DDOT), Human Resources Division, and works closely with the Analytics, Asset, and Performance Management Branch within the Innovation and Performance Division.

The incumbent in this position is responsible for performing analysis and research on DDOT and Human Resources policy, projects, programs, and strategic planning processes. Their duties include identifying emerging trends in regulated industries and developing resources and processes to enable the successful implementation of HR initiatives. The incumbent will be tasked with conducting in-depth data analysis, visualization, and research to facilitate the effective implementation of HR initiatives within DDOT.

Duties And Responsibilities

Incumbent serves as a Data Analyst tasked with overseeing the planning and management of data systems to facilitate data acquisition, storage, retrieval, analysis, reporting, and practical application. The position involves managing complex data and datasets with a high level of proficiency, which includes tasks such as identifying, extracting, integrating, and analyzing data to support various Human Resource projects, initiatives, and tasks. Incumbent provides data visualization and various data analysis services, including but not limited to data mining, exploratory data analysis, data visualization, and report development. This work frequently involves data cleaning, transformation, validation, and modeling, all aimed at gaining insights and drawing conclusions from data to inform decision-making processes.

Performs initial analysis to assess the quality of the data; to determine the meaning of the data; and to provide additional data screening. Incumbent analyzes and defines data requirements and specifications; designs, develops, implements, modifies, and manages databases; ensuring the accuracy and accessibility of data sources. Provides technical expertise in data analysis, business intelligence tools, data visualization, and systems analysis and design. Interprets data; analyzes results, using statistical techniques; and provides ongoing reports.

Qualifications And Education

Individuals must possess one (1) year of specialized experience equivalent to the grade 12 level. Specialized experience is the experience which is directly related to the position and has equipped the person with the knowledge, skills, and abilities to successfully perform the duties of the position, examples of specialized experience may include: advanced data analysis and visualization skills, extensive project management experience, and excellent communication skills. Proficiency in Tableau, Python, and ESRI ArcGIS products is highly preferred.

Bachelor's degree in Data Science, Information System, Human Resources, Business Administration, Industrial Psychology, or related field preferred

Working Conditions/Environment

Work is primarily conducted in an office setting.

Other Significant Facts

Tour of Duty:
Varies

CS-0301-13

Promotion Potential:
No Known Promotion Potential

Duration of Appointment:
Career Service – Regular

Position Designation:
This position will be subject to enhanced suitability screening pursuant to Chapter 4 of DC Personnel Regulations, Suitability - Security Sensitive
Accordingly, the incumbent will be subject to pre-employment checks (criminal background checks, consumer credit check, traffic record checks, if applicable) as a condition of employment, and will be subject to periodic criminal background checks for the duration of your tenure.

Essential Designation:
This position is classified as an essential
position under the provisions of the District Personnel Manual Chapter 12. As such, the incumbent is required to serve in emergency situations to perform critical duties, i.e., snow removal, debris removal, transportation, shelter, operations, food distribution, and communications. These duties may be performed when the government is closed or when employees are dismissed early.

jobs.description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Professional Program Coordinator based in United States.

This remote role provides administrative and coordination support across professional membership, education, continuing education, and major professional events.

You will help keep recurring workflows, schedules, communications, reporting, and program requirements organized and on track.

The position works closely with internal teams, healthcare professionals, volunteers, vendors, and other stakeholders.

It offers an opportunity to contribute to programs that support healthcare professionals and advance professional education.

Success in the role requires strong organization, accuracy, responsiveness, and the ability to manage competing priorities.

You will also support digital events, customer service activities, content workflows, and continuing education processes.

This is a collaborative, deadline-driven environment suited to a resourceful coordinator who enjoys varied responsibilities.

Accountabilities

Coordinate administrative activities across professional membership, professional education, continuing education, and annual conference initiatives.
Manage scheduling for meetings, podcast recordings, and other activities involving healthcare professionals with complex calendars.
Prepare and coordinate monthly team reporting and maintain accurate program information and records.
Coordinate content calendars and publishing activities for professional social media channels.
Monitor and respond to customer service inquiries through Salesforce and ensure requests are handled appropriately.
Support timelines, administrative processes, and coordination requirements for the annual professional conference.
Process vendor payments, volunteer reimbursements, and other financial administration activities.
Collect required continuing education speaker documentation and maintain accurate faculty and program rosters.
Support the dissemination and tracking of continuing education peer-review activities.
Build and maintain monthly continuing education activities within the designated professional education resource center.
Provide editorial workflow and administrative support for professional publications.
Provide technical coordination and support for virtual events, including educational sessions, podcast recordings, and member calls.
Take on additional administrative and program coordination responsibilities as needed while maintaining professionalism, accuracy, and confidentiality.

Requirements

Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university preferred.
2–3 years of relevant office or administrative experience preferred, ideally including experience supporting healthcare professionals.
Experience in project coordination or program management is desirable.
Advanced organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple projects, recurring workflows, deadlines, and priorities simultaneously.
Strong attention to detail and a high level of accuracy when managing data, schedules, documentation, and administrative processes.
Excellent interpersonal skills and the ability to build productive relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, combined with a customer-service-oriented approach.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, word processing tools, and Outlook Calendar.
Ability to work independently, establish priorities, manage deadlines, and remain effective under time pressure.
Resourceful and collaborative approach, with the ability to contribute effectively both independently and as part of a team.
Professionalism, discretion, integrity, and sound judgment when handling sensitive information and stakeholder interactions.
Comfortable providing technical support for virtual meetings and digital events.
Willingness to travel approximately once annually, including occasional overnight travel if required.

Benefits

Salary: $25–$49 per hour, with actual compensation based on relevant experience and qualifications.
Remote work: U.S.-based remote position with flexibility.
Paid time off: Vacation, sick leave, and holidays.
Healthcare: Medical, dental, and vision insurance.
Retirement: 403(b) retirement plan with matching contributions.
Financial support: Flexible spending accounts for eligible healthcare and dependent-care expenses.
Insurance: Life insurance coverage.
Employee support: Access to confidential counseling and resources through an Employee Assistance Program.
Commuter benefits: Support for eligible transit and parking expenses.
Referral program: Opportunities to earn rewards for successful employee referrals.
Inclusive culture: A collaborative workplace focused on diversity, respect, inclusion, and professional growth.
Mission-driven environment: Opportunity to support programs serving healthcare professionals and contributing to broader health-focused initiatives.

The final decision and next steps (interviews, assessments) are managed by their internal team.

jobs.title: Project Coordinator - Professional Services
jobs.description:
Help Us Change the Way People Use Technology

At DGR Systems, we’re about connecting companies to the right solutions and enabling them to gain the most value from their investments. We go to great lengths to hire great people because, at our core, our clients deserve to have each person working on their project bring qualified expertise, a can-do attitude, and experience-based strategic insights to the table. They need to trust their IT consulting firm as a partner who is there to help accelerate their success and not pass them off to a junior team after the contract has been signed. Want to join us?

THE ROLE

DGR Systems designs and delivers technology solutions that our clients rely on to run their organizations. Behind every successful engagement is strong coordination. Projects need to start with the right information, stay organized as work progresses, and close with accurate documentation and financial records.

This role goes beyond administrative support. You will own the intake and setup of new projects, support active engagements across the PMO, and grow into independently manage smaller, clearly scoped engagements.

You will report to the PMO Leader and work alongside DGR's Project Managers and technical delivery teams. This is a hands-on role that directly supports both the client experience and the teams delivering the work.

WHY THIS ISN’T A STANDARD COORDINATOR JOB

This role is designed for someone who wants more than a task-based coordination position. Project Coordinators at DGR are expected to understand what is happening across the engagement, stay ahead of open items, and gradually take on more ownership as their experience grows.

The Project Coordinator plays an important role at the beginning of every new engagement. You will set projects up in our systems, confirm that the right information and documentation are in place, and coordinate the transition from sales into delivery. As projects move forward, you will stay connected with Project Managers, technical teams, Finance, and clients to help keep work organized and moving

The work is varied and often moves quickly. Strong coordination at the beginning of an engagement prevents problems later, and consistent follow-through helps Project Managers and technical teams stay focused on delivery.

The Project Coordinator is an operational part of the delivery team. The work may happen behind the scenes at times, but its impact is visible throughout the engagement.

What You’ll Own

This role covers two things that have to work together for any engagement to start and finish cleanly.

The Setup

Coordinate the intake and setup of new projects: create and configure records in DGR's systems before delivery begins
Confirm that each engagement has the documentation, approvals, contacts, and statements of work it needs before the team kicks off
Coordinate the transition of new engagements from sales to the delivery team, making sure key information, commitments, and next steps are clear before delivery begins
Submit billing triggers and project milestone updates to Finance at the right points in each engagement lifecycle
Keep operational records, templates, trackers, and shared documentation current and organized

The Engagements

Support Project Managers on active engagements by tracking action items, maintaining documentation, and keeping schedules current
Manage the full project lifecycle independently on smaller, clearly scoped engagements, including direct client communication
Coordinate across PMs, technical resources, Finance, and client contacts to keep active work moving and make sure the right people have the information they need
Follow up with responsible parties until commitments close. Follow up on open commitments through completion rather than assuming a request is finished once it has been sent
Surface scheduling conflicts, missing information, overdue items, and delivery risks to the PM or PMO Leader early enough for the team to respond

You will also keep project records current throughout each engagement, not as a milestone activity but as an ongoing standard. If you went unavailable tomorrow, another team member should be able to pick up any active engagement without calling you first. Keeping that record current is part of the daily work, not something saved for the end of the project.

How We Work

Keep the project record current. Conversations, decisions, risks, and next steps need to make their way into the project record so the team is working from the same information. If it's outdated, someone is working from the wrong picture. Keeping the record current is not administrative overhead. It is how we protect delivery and protect our clients.
Follow through to completion. Sending an email, meeting invitation, or request is only the first step. You are expected to follow up, confirm next steps, and make sure important actions reach resolution.
We adjust the level of coordination to the needs of the engagement. A short, focused project should not require the same level of administration as a complex, multi-phase effort. Part of developing in this role is learning to recognize the difference.
The details matter because they affect delivery. Accurate setup, timely follow-up, current documentation, and billing coordination all contribute to a better experience for our clients and delivery teams. The Coordinator often has an opportunity to catch a problem early, before it affects the project or the client, and more importantly, the ability to act on it quickly to prevent it from becoming a larger issue.

What We’re Looking For

You'll

Need

1 to 2 years of professional experience in project coordination, operations, client service, administrative support, or a similar role. Relevant internships may also qualify.
Strong follow-through and the habit of staying with open actions until they are resolved.
Documentation discipline. The ability to leave a record someone else can follow without asking you for context.
Clear, professional written and verbal communication with both technical and non-technical people.
Comfort working in Microsoft 365, particularly Outlook, Teams, SharePoint, and Excel.

It Will Help If You Have

Experience supporting project managers, technical consultants, or delivery teams in a technology or professional services environment
Familiarity with project management, ticketing, or professional services automation tools
Experience with time tracking, billing support, purchase orders, or service-related financial processes
Experience supporting multiple priorities, projects, or client engagements at the same time

We'll

Teach You

How DGR Project Managers and Technical Leads work together to deliver client engagements
DGR's delivery methodologies and how they apply to different engagement types
DGR's service portfolio, technology partners, and the types of client environments we support
Our tooling, systems, documentation standards, and coordination workflows

Who This Isn’t For

We want you to have a clear picture of what will make someone successful in this role.

This role works best for someone who is comfortable learning an established process and then taking the next reasonable step without needing every routine action assigned.
Follow-through is a major part of the role. Success here requires staying engaged with open actions until they are completed or appropriately escalated.
This position carries more operational responsibility than a traditional administrative coordinator role. The work directly affects project delivery and the client experience.
The work changes frequently across clients and technology areas, so this role is best suited for someone who enjoys variety and can stay organized while managing several priorities at once.

YOUR PATH FORWARD

The Project Coordinator role is the starting point for DGR's PMO career ladder. If you want to grow into a Project Manager, Senior Project Manager, or beyond, this role is how that path begins at DGR. For employees interested in that path, the role provides opportunities to build the client, delivery, and project management skills needed to grow into a Project Manager.

Career progression is based on demonstrated capability, judgment, delivery quality, and readiness for greater ownership rather than time in role alone. The Coordinators who advance are the ones who treat every engagement, large or small, with the same standard of care. For someone interested in building a career in project management or technology consulting delivery, this role provides a practical starting point with increasing responsibility over time.

Compensation & Benefits

Base salary range

$52,000 - $68,000

Work arrangement

-

Tampa area

DGR Systems also offers a robust company benefits package designed to support employees and their families, including compettive health and welfare benefits, paid time off, 401k, Health Savings Account, certification reimbursement, and other company-sponsored programs.

How To Apply For This Role

Send us your resume and a few sentences about a time you had to keep something moving when information was missing, responsibilities were unclear, or something did not go according to plan. Tell us what you did and how the situation turned out. We are more interested in how you approached the situation than whether everything went perfectly.

Apply to:

joinus@dgrsystems.com

DGR Systems is an equal opportunity employer. We consider all qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic.

We are interested in every qualified candidate who is eligible to work in the United States. However, we are not able to sponsor visas.

Job Summary

This position is in the District Department of Transportation (DDOT), Human Resources Division, and works closely with the Analytics, Asset, and Performance Management Branch within the Innovation and Performance Division.

The incumbent in this position is responsible for performing analysis and research on DDOT and Human Resources policy, projects, programs, and strategic planning processes. Their duties include identifying emerging trends in regulated industries and developing resources and processes to enable the successful implementation of HR initiatives. The incumbent will be tasked with conducting in-depth data analysis, visualization, and research to facilitate the effective implementation of HR initiatives within DDOT.

Duties And Responsibilities

Incumbent serves as a Data Analyst tasked with overseeing the planning and management of data systems to facilitate data acquisition, storage, retrieval, analysis, reporting, and practical application. The position involves managing complex data and datasets with a high level of proficiency, which includes tasks such as identifying, extracting, integrating, and analyzing data to support various Human Resource projects, initiatives, and tasks. Incumbent provides data visualization and various data analysis services, including but not limited to data mining, exploratory data analysis, data visualization, and report development. This work frequently involves data cleaning, transformation, validation, and modeling, all aimed at gaining insights and drawing conclusions from data to inform decision-making processes.

Performs initial analysis to assess the quality of the data; to determine the meaning of the data; and to provide additional data screening. Incumbent analyzes and defines data requirements and specifications; designs, develops, implements, modifies, and manages databases; ensuring the accuracy and accessibility of data sources. Provides technical expertise in data analysis, business intelligence tools, data visualization, and systems analysis and design. Interprets data; analyzes results, using statistical techniques; and provides ongoing reports.

Qualifications And Education

Individuals must possess one (1) year of specialized experience equivalent to the grade 12 level. Specialized experience is the experience which is directly related to the position and has equipped the person with the knowledge, skills, and abilities to successfully perform the duties of the position, examples of specialized experience may include: advanced data analysis and visualization skills, extensive project management experience, and excellent communication skills. Proficiency in Tableau, Python, and ESRI ArcGIS products is highly preferred.

Bachelor's degree in Data Science, Information System, Human Resources, Business Administration, Industrial Psychology, or related field preferred

new_jobs.title: Project Coordinator - Professional Services
new_jobs.description:
Help Us Change the Way People Use Technology

At DGR Systems, we’re about connecting companies to the right solutions and enabling them to gain the most value from their investments. We go to great lengths to hire great people because, at our core, our clients deserve to have each person working on their project bring qualified expertise, a can-do attitude, and experience-based strategic insights to the table. They need to trust their IT consulting firm as a partner who is there to help accelerate their success and not pass them off to a junior team after the contract has been signed. Want to join us?

THE ROLE

DGR Systems designs and delivers technology solutions that our clients rely on to run their organizations. Behind every successful engagement is strong coordination. Projects need to start with the right information, stay organized as work progresses, and close with accurate documentation and financial records.

This role goes beyond administrative support. You will own the intake and setup of new projects, support active engagements across the PMO, and grow into independently manage smaller, clearly scoped engagements.

You will report to the PMO Leader and work alongside DGR's Project Managers and technical delivery teams. This is a hands-on role that directly supports both the client experience and the teams delivering the work.

WHY THIS ISN’T A STANDARD COORDINATOR JOB

This role is designed for someone who wants more than a task-based coordination position. Project Coordinators at DGR are expected to understand what is happening across the engagement, stay ahead of open items, and gradually take on more ownership as their experience grows.

The Project Coordinator plays an important role at the beginning of every new engagement. You will set projects up in our systems, confirm that the right information and documentation are in place, and coordinate the transition from sales into delivery. As projects move forward, you will stay connected with Project Managers, technical teams, Finance, and clients to help keep work organized and moving

The work is varied and often moves quickly. Strong coordination at the beginning of an engagement prevents problems later, and consistent follow-through helps Project Managers and technical teams stay focused on delivery.

The Project Coordinator is an operational part of the delivery team. The work may happen behind the scenes at times, but its impact is visible throughout the engagement.

What You’ll Own

This role covers two things that have to work together for any engagement to start and finish cleanly.

The Setup

Coordinate the intake and setup of new projects: create and configure records in DGR's systems before delivery begins
Confirm that each engagement has the documentation, approvals, contacts, and statements of work it needs before the team kicks off
Coordinate the transition of new engagements from sales to the delivery team, making sure key information, commitments, and next steps are clear before delivery begins
Submit billing triggers and project milestone updates to Finance at the right points in each engagement lifecycle
Keep operational records, templates, trackers, and shared documentation current and organized

The Engagements

Support Project Managers on active engagements by tracking action items, maintaining documentation, and keeping schedules current
Manage the full project lifecycle independently on smaller, clearly scoped engagements, including direct client communication
Coordinate across PMs, technical resources, Finance, and client contacts to keep active work moving and make sure the right people have the information they need
Follow up with responsible parties until commitments close. Follow up on open commitments through completion rather than assuming a request is finished once it has been sent
Surface scheduling conflicts, missing information, overdue items, and delivery risks to the PM or PMO Leader early enough for the team to respond

You will also keep project records current throughout each engagement, not as a milestone activity but as an ongoing standard. If you went unavailable tomorrow, another team member should be able to pick up any active engagement without calling you first. Keeping that record current is part of the daily work, not something saved for the end of the project.

How We Work

Keep the project record current. Conversations, decisions, risks, and next steps need to make their way into the project record so the team is working from the same information. If it's outdated, someone is working from the wrong picture. Keeping the record current is not administrative overhead. It is how we protect delivery and protect our clients.
Follow through to completion. Sending an email, meeting invitation, or request is only the first step. You are expected to follow up, confirm next steps, and make sure important actions reach resolution.
We adjust the level of coordination to the needs of the engagement. A short, focused project should not require the same level of administration as a complex, multi-phase effort. Part of developing in this role is learning to recognize the difference.
The details matter because they affect delivery. Accurate setup, timely follow-up, current documentation, and billing coordination all contribute to a better experience for our clients and delivery teams. The Coordinator often has an opportunity to catch a problem early, before it affects the project or the client, and more importantly, the ability to act on it quickly to prevent it from becoming a larger issue.

What We’re Looking For

You'll

Need

1 to 2 years of professional experience in project coordination, operations, client service, administrative support, or a similar role. Relevant internships may also qualify.
Strong follow-through and the habit of staying with open actions until they are resolved.
Documentation discipline. The ability to leave a record someone else can follow without asking you for context.
Clear, professional written and verbal communication with both technical and non-technical people.
Comfort working in Microsoft 365, particularly Outlook, Teams, SharePoint, and Excel.

It Will Help If You Have

Experience supporting project managers, technical consultants, or delivery teams in a technology or professional services environment
Familiarity with project management, ticketing, or professional services automation tools
Experience with time tracking, billing support, purchase orders, or service-related financial processes
Experience supporting multiple priorities, projects, or client engagements at the same time

We'll

Teach You

How DGR Project Managers and Technical Leads work together to deliver client engagements
DGR's delivery methodologies and how they apply to different engagement types
DGR's service portfolio, technology partners, and the types of client environments we support
Our tooling, systems, documentation standards, and coordination workflows

Who This Isn’t For

We want you to have a clear picture of what will make someone successful in this role.

This role works best for someone who is comfortable learning an established process and then taking the next reasonable step without needing every routine action assigned.
Follow-through is a major part of the role. Success here requires staying engaged with open actions until they are completed or appropriately escalated.
This position carries more operational responsibility than a traditional administrative coordinator role. The work directly affects project delivery and the client experience.
The work changes frequently across clients and technology areas, so this role is best suited for someone who enjoys variety and can stay organized while managing several priorities at once.

YOUR PATH FORWARD

The Project Coordinator role is the starting point for DGR's PMO career ladder. If you want to grow into a Project Manager, Senior Project Manager, or beyond, this role is how that path begins at DGR. For employees interested in that path, the role provides opportunities to build the client, delivery, and project management skills needed to grow into a Project Manager.

Career progression is based on demonstrated capability, judgment, delivery quality, and readiness for greater ownership rather than time in role alone. The Coordinators who advance are the ones who treat every engagement, large or small, with the same standard of care. For someone interested in building a career in project management or technology consulting delivery, this role provides a practical starting point with increasing responsibility over time.

Compensation & Benefits

Base salary range

$52,000 - $68,000

Work arrangement

-

Tampa area

DGR Systems also offers a robust company benefits package designed to support employees and their families, including compettive health and welfare benefits, paid time off, 401k, Health Savings Account, certification reimbursement, and other company-sponsored programs.

How To Apply For This Role

Send us your resume and a few sentences about a time you had to keep something moving when information was missing, responsibilities were unclear, or something did not go according to plan. Tell us what you did and how the situation turned out. We are more interested in how you approached the situation than whether everything went perfectly.
